newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sale of major Australian power station imminent.
newsitem.headline: Sale of major Australian power station imminent.

text.p: The sale of Australia's big Loy Yang A power station in Victoria state is expected to be announced within days, possibly as early as the weekend, sources close to the bidders said.
One source, who declined to be named, told Reuters the sale of the 2,000 megawatt station and associated coal mine was likely to fetch around A$4.5 billion for the state government.
This compares with a value of around A$5 billion quoted in recent newspaper reports.
"I would have thought five (billion dollars) was optimistic -- very optimistic, particularly with the rise in interest rates," the source said.
Final bids for Loy Yang A, the biggest and most modern power station to be privatised by the Victoria government, must be lodged by close of business on Thursday.
Three major consortia are reported in local media to be strong bidders, all led by U.S. utilities.
NRG Energy Inc and CMS Energy Corp are reported to have teamed with British Energy Plc and Australian investment bank Macquarie Bank in one consortium.
Another consortium is led by the AES Corp and a third by the American Electric Power Co Inc.
The Victoria government has so far sold over A$13 billion worth of electricity assets in an effort to create a competitive power industry, to retire debt and win a further credit upgrade.
The government expects Loy Yang A to be sold for over A$4 billion, a spokesman told Reuters.
But the sale will be a complex transaction and is likely to require a week before the winning bid is announced, he said.
"In all reality, we will be looking at maybe a week," the spokesman said.
